label: distinctIndex is narrowed to a byte on the way across
find:
for (i = 0; i < V90_CONSTELLATIONS; i++)
		params->distinctIndex[i] = cp->distinctIndex[i];
replace:
for (i = 0; i < V90_CONSTELLATIONS; i++)
		params->distinctIndex[i] = (int)(unsigned char)cp->distinctIndex[i];
why: THE STORE IS THIRTY-TWO BITS AND THE FIXTURE CANNOT SEE IT, BY ITS OWN CHOICE.  The object copies a whole word -- `mov 0x28(%edi,%edx,4),%esi ; mov %esi,0x638(%ecx,%edx,4)` at .text+0x33cbe -- so the width is settled from the instructions and not from this tier.  It cannot be settled here because the same field also SCALES THE MASK BASE by sixteen (`shl $0x4` then `lea 0x42(...)`), so any trial whose `word_28[i]` did not fit in a byte would read outside both mask blocks; the blob does that too, but it is undefined in the reconstruction and a trial that reaches undefined behaviour is not a trial (D561).  Every trial therefore keeps `word_28` in 0..5, where the narrowed and the wide spelling agree byte for byte.  The row is kept rather than deleted because it names exactly which claim rests on the disassembly alone.

label: the loop bound is spelled with the SOURCE's macro rather than the destination's
find:
for (i = 0; i < V90_CONSTELLATIONS; i++)
		params->distinctIndex[i] = cp->distinctIndex[i];
replace:
for (i = 0; i < V92CP_GROUPS; i++)
		params->distinctIndex[i] = cp->distinctIndex[i];
why: V90_CONSTELLATIONS AND V92CP_GROUPS ARE BOTH 6, AND THE OBJECT CANNOT SEPARATE THEM.  The loop reads `cp->word_28[i]`, which has V92CP_GROUPS entries, and writes `params->distinctIndex[i]`, which has V90_CONSTELLATIONS -- so either macro is defensible and the object emits one immediate, `cmp $0x5 ; jbe` at .text+0x33cca, for both.  V90_CONSTELLATIONS is chosen because the loop's purpose is to fill the destination block, and V90MappingParams.h derives its 6 from the three getters' own `cmpl $0x5` while V92CP.h derives its 6 from the packer's `add $0x10` and the two blocks' spacing.  A mutation that changes the VALUE -- the row above -- is not equivalent and is caught.

why: WHICH END THE GATE IS READ FROM IS A CODEGEN FACT AND NO TEST CAN SEE IT FROM ONE CALL.  Step 1 writes `params->word_61c = (cp->byte_24 != 0)` and nothing between there and this loop touches +0x61c -- `constellation` ends at +0x304, `codecConstellation` at +0x604 and `constellationSize` at +0x61c exactly, and no table store can pass its own 128-byte extent -- so the destination's copy is a faithful 0/1 image of the source byte on every trial and both spellings choose the same arm.  What separates them is a CALLER that scribbles on `params->word_61c` between two calls, and this function has no caller in the object to do that (zero relocations name it).  The object settles it anyway: .text+0x33d71 reloads the CP pointer from the stack and +0x33d75 is `cmpb $0x0,0x24(%ecx)`, both INSIDE the loop the back edge at +0x33e82 closes, so the SOURCE is re-read on every iteration.  That is the V.90 twin's behaviour (finding F7570) and the opposite of V92setParamsInfoFromCPUnPck's three gates, which read back the destination's copies.
